cluster_name: Brazil STF justices clash over Federal Police director removal
event_summary: STF Justice André Mendonça petitioned to remove Federal Police Director Andrei Rodrigues on September 9, 2026; the Supreme Court's Second Panel split on the vote before Justice Gilmar Mendes suspended proceedings with a 'vista,' while the AGU counter-petitioned Justice Fachin to block the removal.
tldr: The cluster is dominated by a sharp intra-STF confrontation: conservative Justice André Mendonça (a Bolsonaro appointee) moved to oust Federal Police Director Andrei Rodrigues, producing a split Second Panel vote before Gilmar Mendes froze proceedings by requesting 'vista.' Former President Michel Temer then publicly urged Justice Moraes — his own STF appointee — to seek dialogue with Mendonça, a rare ex-presidential intervention that O Globo treated as the story's centre of gravity. Brazilian outlets simultaneously embedded the legal crisis in the 2026 electoral backdrop, with BBC Brasil publishing an interactive presidential-candidates guide and Carta Capital noting Lula's 30-point polling lead in Bahia the same day. Non-Brazilian items in the cluster (Haaretz daily cartoon, N1 Serbia live-stream link, Reason metadata artefact, G1 Globo broadcast notices) carry no substantive relation to the Brazil story and appear to be false-clustered noise.

BBC Brasil simultaneously covers the PF director crisis and a 2026 presidential-candidate policy guide, embedding the institutional dispute within a pre-election context no other outlet in the cluster explicitly makes.

Carta Capital (centre-left investigative) pairs its Lula-Bolsonaro polling item with a Ziyech-to-Botafogo sports transfer story — the only non-political item from a Brazilian news outlet, suggesting miscellaneous clustering.

Reason's item is a metadata extraction failure (title: 'Screenshot 2026-09-04 155533'); the linked article covers RFK Jr.'s MAHA cooking show as government propaganda — entirely unrelated to the Brazilian institutional crisis.

Both G1 Globo items are live-broadcast schedule links for regional affiliates (Juiz de Fora and Divinópolis), carrying no news content — feed artefacts that inflated the cluster's Brazil article count.

bottom_line: This cluster captures a genuine Brazilian constitutional flashpoint — STF Justice Mendonça's move to remove the Federal Police chief, blocked mid-vote by Gilmar Mendes and counter-petitioned by the AGU — set against the 2026 election year's charged institutional backdrop. A significant portion of the cluster's articles (live-broadcast links, a daily cartoon, a metadata artefact) are pipeline noise rather than editorial coverage, which limits the analytical signal to Brazilian Portuguese outlets.
